title: The 90-Minute Core
summary: Use this on ordinary days. Keep transitions short and use a timer.

title: Rest and Injury Prevention
summary: This is preventive guidance, not medical diagnosis.

title: Weekly Schedule
summary: Keep one main technical focus for a week while changing its musical application. This gives repetition without mindless sameness.

title: Bending, Vibrato, Dynamics, and Harmonics
summary: This is the expressive center of the system. Accuracy without character is unfinished; character without pitch control is unreliable.

title: Clean Speed System
summary: Speed is the result of efficient motion, accurate timing, reliable muting, and gradual exposure—not maximum effort.

title: Legato and Tapping
summary: Create connected notes with deliberate rhythm and equal musical authority—not merely softer attacks between picked notes.

title: Picking and Synchronization
summary: Make pick attack, fretting contact, release, and muting arrive as one rhythmic event across strings.

title: Sweeping, String Skipping, and Muting
summary: Cross nonadjacent and adjacent strings efficiently while each note remains rhythmically separate and unwanted strings stay silent.

title: Funk and Muted Articulation
summary: Develop the percussive control needed for Wonderful Slippery Thing-style grooves, clean funk, neo-soul, and rhythmically alive lead playing.

title: Odd Meter and Rhythmic Displacement
summary: Feel unusual groupings as phrases rather than perform arithmetic while playing.

title: Time, Subdivisions, and the Metronome
summary: Own the space between clicks so the metronome confirms your pulse rather than creating it.

title: Famous Short Melodies and Riffs — Learn by Ear

title: Hearing Chords and Bass Lines
summary: Stop treating a solo as notes floating over an anonymous backing. Hear where harmony moves and why a melodic note feels stable, bright, dark, tense, or resolved.

title: The No-Tabs Method

title: Transcription Ladder
summary: Move up when the process is reliable, not when one lucky song works.

title: Fretboard Freedom
summary: The neck is not five boxes. It is one pitch map viewed through intervals, chord tones, and sound.

title: How Chords Are Built
summary: Chord creation is interval selection plus voicing and context. You never need to wait for a chord dictionary.

title: How Scales Are Built

title: Modes, Harmony, and Playing Through Changes

title: Seventh Chords, Extensions, and Alterations
summary: Extensions work because a chord may continue stacking thirds: 9, 11, 13. On guitar, choose the tones the ear needs.

title: Triads, Inversions, and Voice Leading
summary: Turn the whole neck into small movable harmony and create smooth chord movement useful for funk, neo-soul, fusion, accompaniment, and melodic soloing.

title: Build Your Own Vocabulary
summary: Vocabulary should become grammar you can recombine, not quotations pasted into unrelated conversations.

title: Motif Development
summary: A motif is a small recognizable identity—often rhythm plus contour, not a specific lick.

title: Target Notes and Chord Changes
summary: Make the harmony audible through melodic arrival while preserving rhythm and phrase continuity.

title: Tension, Release, and Outside Playing
summary: Outside playing works when the listener can hear where “inside” is and believes you meant to leave and return.

title: The Musical Sentence
summary: Improvisation becomes understandable when phrases behave like speech: ideas, breath, emphasis, response, development, and conclusion.

title: Self-Made Cover Rules — No Tabs First
summary: Your first complete version comes from the recording, your ears, and your musical decisions. A tab may later diagnose differences, but it cannot design your interpretation.

title: Guthrie Study Map
summary: Study Guthrie as a problem-solver. Learn small sections, identify the principle, then make it yours.

title: Develop Your Own Voice
summary: Your voice is not found by avoiding influences. It appears when influences pass through your ears, taste, limitations, experiences, and repeated choices.

title: Natural Stage Banter
summary: Being funny like Guthrie does not mean copying Guthrie's jokes. His strongest lesson is comfort, observation, timing, vocabulary, and treating the audience like intelligent humans.

title: 24-Week Final Performance

title: Baseline Test

title: Monthly Tests
summary: Run at the end of weeks 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, and 24. Use the same recording setup and compare to your baseline, not to a polished artist recording.
